records.name: Interfaith Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps people of different faiths understand each other through talks, classes, community walks, and youth programs. Neighbors can attend the fall public events or join the newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Go to a talk, take part in the Walk for Understanding fundraiser, or sign up for an interfaith leadership class.

schedule.text: Public programs through fall 2026, including the Walk for Understanding on October 18 (2:00 pm), talks on October 25 and 27, and a November 15 event at Congregation Mikveh Israel. Some events are virtual.

cost.text: Varies by event; check each registration link

first_step.how: Pick an event on the website and use its Register link, or sign up for the newsletter
first_step.basis: Public events each have a registration link and a newsletter sign up is offered, so a newcomer has a clear way in

records.notes: Event prices are not on the fetched page. The contact email is behind a protected link and was not recorded. A 2026 photo post and an Interfaith Youth Neighborhood Mosaic program appeared in search snippets only; not verified.

records.name: Gloria Dei (Old Swedes') Church Community Meal Prep
records.summary: Church members and friends who cook a meal every other month for St. Gabriel's Episcopal Church in North Philadelphia, a neighborhood outreach. Anyone can come help cook and serve.
records.what_you_do: Help cook and get a meal ready in the church kitchen on a weeknight evening.

schedule.text: Every other month on a Wednesday evening, 6:30 to 9 pm. Listed dates were June 3, 2026 and July 29, 2026.

cost.text: No cost mentioned on the event page

first_step.how: RSVP to Christine Pickup if you can, or just show up. General church line: 215-389-1513 or info@old-swedes.org
first_step.basis: The event page invites people to just show up and gives a way to RSVP

records.notes: The page says the church's meal is one of a network of churches that serves meals every week. The July 29, 2026 date is listed but no page confirms it ran. Church phone and email are from the general contact on the site. Episcopal is recorded under protestant because the faith list has no Episcopal id.

records.name: First Presbyterian Church Casserole Volunteers
records.summary: A Center City church that gathers volunteers after Sunday worship to assemble casseroles for the University City Hospitality Coalition's free meals. The work takes less than an hour and includes time to visit.
records.what_you_do: Assemble 30 to 40 casseroles in Old Buttonwood Hall, then stay for fellowship.

schedule.text: Sunday mornings after the 10 am combined worship service on listed dates. Dates shown: June 14, 2026 (10 to 10:45 am) and August 16, 2026 (11:45 am to 12:30 pm).

cost.text: Not mentioned on the event page

first_step.how: Email Laura Colee at laura.colee@fpcphila.org to volunteer for the next date
first_step.basis: Volunteers are invited and a named contact is listed, but eligibility and sign up steps are not spelled out

records.notes: Both event pages list a single date and do not say whether the event repeats. Volunteer work supports the University City Hospitality Coalition record in this file.

records.name: University City Hospitality Coalition
records.summary: A volunteer-run group that serves free hot meals and sandwiches to people in West Philadelphia's University City, with church and campus partners hosting the meals. It also works to ease hunger and homelessness in the neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Help cook, assemble meals, or bake at partner churches, or donate food. Partner churches post their volunteer days.

schedule.text: Hot meals on weeknights at 6:00 pm at rotating church and campus sites, and a Saturday noon meal, per an undated PA 211 listing. Confirm before going.

first_step.how: Volunteer through a partner church's posted volunteer day, or call the coordinators before a shift to confirm the schedule

records.notes: The group's website, uc-hc.org, listed on Idealist, did not resolve when fetched (DNS error), so no website is recorded. Schedules conflict: the undated PA 211 listing and a 2024 city flyer name different sites. The 2016 brochure lists a different phone and email, not used. Mailing address per Idealist: P.O. Box 7846, Philadelphia, PA 19101. Re-check the schedule before publishing.

records.name: Tribe 12
records.summary: A Jewish community in Philadelphia for people in their 20s and 30s. It runs social events such as caramel apple making, frame drumming, and holiday and Shabbat gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a calendar event, such as a cooking night or a drumming session, and meet other young adults.

schedule.text: Events through the month. Listed dates include Caramel Apple Making on Thursday, October 15, 2026 (6:30 to 8:30 pm) and Frame Drumming on Wednesday, October 21, 2026 (7 to 8:30 pm).

cost.text: Event prices not listed on the home page. An optional sustainer gift of $12 a month is offered.

first_step.how: Choose an event on the events calendar and register. Some events are marked space limited.
first_step.basis: Single events are open to registration on a public calendar, but the page does not say newcomers are especially welcome

records.notes: Eligibility is for people in their 20s and 30s; the home page does not say whether older or younger people can attend, so open_to is public with that age focus. A search snippet described a monthly Shabbat dinner; the fetched home page did not confirm it, so it is not recorded. Event locations are not on the home page.

records.name: First Unitarian Church of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Unitarian Universalist congregation on Chestnut Street. It holds Sunday services in person and on Zoom, and has a New Here path for visitors.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Sunday service, join the 20s and 30s group, or take part in adult spirit and learning programs.

schedule.text: Sunday worship, in person and on Zoom. The next listed service is Sunday, October 11, 2026 at 11 am with Rev. Abbey Tennis.

cost.text: Not listed on the pages checked

first_step.how: Read What to Expect Sunday Morning on the website, or fill out the new visitor card
first_step.basis: The website has a New Here section that explains what to expect, a visitor card, and a path to membership

records.notes: Adult Spirit+Ed and the 20s and 30s group are listed on the site, but their days, times and descriptions were not published on the pages checked. The site gives a contact page rather than an email address. Fax number not recorded.

records.name: St. Michael's Lutheran Church, Germantown (Holy Hot Dish meal)
records.summary: A Germantown congregation that once served a free Saturday community meal. Not joinable: the congregation is reported closed.
records.notes: A 2010 article describes a Saturday meal, 11 am to 1 pm, at 6671 Germantown Ave. A later report describes a farewell service marking 288 years, around 2016. The food directory lists the church as closed. Not verified by the congregation. Re-check before final hide.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls used (hard cap reached). 27 WebFetch calls used. Strongest records come from the groups' own pages (Interfaith Philadelphia, Old Swedes, First Unitarian, Tribe 12, First Presbyterian). The University City Hospitality Coalition record is low confidence: its own site did not resolve and the schedules conflict across sources. The St. Michael's record is a hide (defunct) based on a 2016 closure report and a closed directory listing. Many faith leads with their own websites (Broad Street Ministry, Old St. Joe's, Tindley Temple, the FIGHT guide congregations, the Quaker, Buddhist and Hindu temples) still need fetches; they are in leads_only because the URL to each group's own site was not confirmed in search results and the search cap ended the run. Next run should start from these leads_only items.
